$documentation: ADVISORY ALLOWLIST for the release auto-tagger (flair#1890).
Condition 9 of scripts/release-auto-tag.mjs refuses a release whose checks are
not all on the whitelist success|neutral|skipped. This file is the ONE
exception: a check named here may fail (or be non-success in any way) without
refusing the release; those failures are still listed in the run summary.
Matching is by EXACT NAME, which is the whole point. Check names are chosen by
the workflows in this repo, so a merged PR could rename a failing check to
look advisory (name it 'x (advisory)') — a suffix or substring match would
silently widen the exception. Only the strings below are tolerated, and a
check whose name merely ENDS in '(advisory)' but is not listed here still
refuses (asserted by test/unit/release-auto-tag.test.ts).
Seed (2026-09-25): derived from the checks on main's HEAD that this repo
declares advisory-only. The repo's standing rule (see the PROMOTION CRITERION
comment in .github/workflows/test.yml) is that an advisory-only check carries
the marker '(advisory)' in its own name AND, at its definition, (a) what
would make it blocking and (b) when that is re-evaluated. Exactly one check
on main carries that marker today, so this list has exactly one entry:
- 'launchd adopt-then-upgrade (macOS, advisory)'
(test.yml job launchd-adopt-upgrade-darwin; blocking when #1685 lands).
ADDING AN ENTRY IS A REVIEWED ACT. Deleting it once the check becomes
blocking is the point of listing it here rather than in the workflow.
